questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B. 
 Column A Column B 
 A. Acids 1. Produce OH⁻ ions in water 
 B. Bases 2. Produce H⁺ (or H₃O⁺) ions in water 
 C. Acid + Base 3. Form salt and water (neutralisation) 
 D. Both conduct electricity 4. Due to presence of ions in solution 
2f:T93
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A-2; B-1; C-3; D-4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acids and Hydrogen Ions (A-2)**: According to the **Arrhenius theory**, an **acid** is a substance that dissociates in water to yield **hydrogen ions (H+)**. Since **H+** ions cannot exist alone, they combine with water molecules to form **hydronium ions (H3O+)**. ***Hence, A matches with 2 is correct.***
 
• **Bases and Hydroxide Ions (B-1)**: A **base** is defined as a substance that, when dissolved in water, increases the concentration of **hydroxide ions (OH-)**. Bases that are soluble in water are specifically called **alkalis**. ***Hence, B matches with 1 is correct.***
 
• **Neutralization Reaction (C-3)**: When an **acid** reacts with a **base**, the **H+** ions of the acid react with the **OH-** ions of the base to form **water (H2O)** and a **salt**. This chemical reaction is known as **Neutralization** and is typically **exothermic** in nature. ***Hence, C matches with 3 is correct.***
 
• **Electrical Conductivity (D-4)**: Both **acids** and **bases** in their **aqueous solutions** are capable of conducting **electricity**. This conductivity is attributed to the presence of **free ions** (cations and anions) in the solution, which act as **charge carriers**. Pure distilled water does not conduct electricity, but the addition of an acid or base provides the necessary **electrolytes**. ***Hence, D matches with 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is A-2; B-1; C-3; D-4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Acids**:
 
 
• Acids have a **sour taste** and turn **blue litmus paper red**.
 
• They have a **pH value** of **less than 7** on the pH scale.
 
• Common examples include **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, **Sulphuric acid (H2SO4)**, and **Citric acid** found in lemons.
 
• **Strong acids** like **HCl** ionize completely in water, while **weak acids** like **acetic acid (vinegar)** ionize only partially.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Bases**:
 
 
• Bases have a **bitter taste** and a **soapy or slippery feel** to the touch.
 
• They turn **red litmus paper blue** and have a **pH value** of **greater than 7**.
 
• Common examples include **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, **Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)**, and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
• Bases are used extensively in the manufacture of **soaps, detergents, and antacids**.
 
 
 
• **The pH Scale**:
 
 
• The **pH scale** was introduced by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909** to measure the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.
 
• The scale ranges from **0 to 14**, where **7 is neutral** (the pH of pure water).
 
• A lower pH signifies a higher concentration of **hydrogen ions**, making the solution more acidic.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indicators**: Substances like **Phenolphthalein** and **Methyl Orange** are used to test for acids and bases. **Phenolphthalein** remains colorless in acid but turns **pink** in basic solutions.
 
• **Universal Indicator**: This is a mixture of several indicators that shows different colors at different concentrations of **hydrogen ions** in a solution, helping determine the approximate **pH value**.
 
• **Strength of Solutions**: The strength of an acid or base depends on the **number of H+ ions** or **OH- ions** produced, respectively. For instance, **1 Molar HCl** is a stronger acid than **1 Molar CH3COOH** because it produces more **H+ ions**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about momentum is true?

options.text: Momentum has both magnitude and direction.
The SI unit of momentum is kilogram per second.
Momentum is the sum of mass and velocity.
Momentum has magnitude only and no direction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Momentum has both magnitude and direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Momentum** is a fundamental concept in physics, defined as the product of an object's **mass** and its **velocity**. It is typically represented by the symbol **p**.
 
• **Statement 1:** Momentum is a **vector quantity**. By definition, a vector quantity is one that has both a **magnitude** (how much) and a **direction** (where it is going). The direction of the momentum vector is the same as the direction of the **velocity** vector. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** The **Standard International (SI) unit** of momentum is the **kilogram-meter per second**, written as **kg·m/s**. The statement claims the unit is kilogram per second, which is incorrect as it lacks the **meter (distance)** component required for velocity. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3:** Mathematically, momentum is calculated as **p = m × v**, where **m** is mass and **v** is velocity. It is the **product** of these two variables, not the sum. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4:** Since momentum is derived from **velocity** (which is a vector), it must have a direction. Only **scalar quantities**, such as **speed** or **mass**, have magnitude only. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Conservation of Momentum:** This is a major law of physics stating that the total momentum of an **isolated system** remains **constant** if no external forces act on it. This principle is vital in analyzing **collisions** and **explosions**.
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:** Sir **Isaac Newton** originally defined his second law in terms of momentum. He stated that the **force** (**F**) acting on an object is equal to the **rate of change of momentum** (**dp/dt**) over **time**.
 
• **Impulse:** The change in momentum is known as **impulse**. It is the product of the average **force** and the **time interval** during which it acts. The units for impulse are **Newton-seconds (N·s)**, which are equivalent to **kg·m/s**.
 
• **Relativistic Momentum:** In **Einstein’s** theory of **special relativity**, as an object's speed approaches the **speed of light**, its momentum increases more rapidly than its velocity, requiring a modified formula that includes the **Lorentz factor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional representation of momentum is **[MLT⁻¹]**, where **M** is Mass, **L** is Length, and **T** is Time.
 
• **Mass vs. Velocity Influence:** A very **heavy object** (like a ship) moving slowly can have the same momentum as a **light object** (like a bullet) moving very fast. 
 
• **Practical Application:** Safety features in **vehicles**, such as **airbags** and **crumple zones**, are designed to increase the **time** it takes for momentum to change during a crash, thereby reducing the **impact force** on the passengers.
 
• **CGS Unit:** In the **Centimetre-Gram-Second** system, the unit of momentum is the **gram-centimetre per second (g·cm/s)**.

questions.question: ​Which of the following best explains the origin of coal and petroleum?

options.text: Compaction of forest wood under sunlight
Decomposition of volcanic rocks under high pressure
Crystallisation of minerals under the seabed
Fossilisation of plants and animals under high temperature and pressure over millions of years

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fossilisation of plants and animals under high temperature and pressure over millions of years**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Fossil fuels** like **coal** and **petroleum** are formed through the biological and chemical transformation of ancient organic matter. 
• **Coal** primarily originates from the remains of **terrestrial plants** and trees that grew in vast **swampy forests** approximately **300 to 360 million years ago** during the **Carboniferous Period**. When these plants died, they were buried under layers of water and dirt, preventing full decay. ***Hence, statement 4 is the most accurate explanation.*** 
• **Petroleum** (crude oil) and **natural gas** are derived from the remains of **microscopic marine organisms**, such as **plankton and algae**. These organisms settled on the **ocean floor** and were covered by sediments like **silt and mud**. 
• The transformation process requires **anaerobic conditions** (absence of oxygen), which ensures that the organic matter does not rot completely but undergoes slow chemical changes. 
• Over **millions of years**, the weight of the accumulating sediment layers creates **high pressure** and generates **high temperature** from the Earth's interior, which eventually converts the buried organic debris into **hydrocarbons**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Classification of Coal**: Based on the degree of compression and carbon content, coal is divided into four main types: **Peat** (lowest carbon), **Lignite** (brown coal), **Bituminous** (most common), and **Anthracite** (hardest coal with over **85% carbon**). 
• **Petroleum Refining**: Crude oil extracted from the ground is a mixture of various hydrocarbons. It is processed in **refineries** using **fractional distillation** to produce **petrol**, **diesel**, **kerosene**, **asphalt**, and **liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)**. 
• **Non-Renewable Resources**: Because the formation of these fuels takes **millions of years**, they are classified as **non-renewable energy sources**. Their current rate of consumption far exceeds the rate of natural replenishment. 
• **Environmental Impact**: The combustion of fossil fuels releases **carbon dioxide (CO2)**, **sulfur dioxide**, and **nitrogen oxides**, which contribute to the **greenhouse effect** and **global warming**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Carbonisation**: The slow chemical process of conversion of dead vegetation into coal is specifically known as **carbonisation**. This happens under conditions of **extreme pressure** and **lack of air**. 
• **Oil Windows**: Petroleum formation typically occurs within a specific temperature range called the **"oil window"** (usually **50°C to 150°C**). If the temperature is higher, the organic matter is further broken down into **natural gas (methane)**. 
• **Geological Traps**: Petroleum is often found trapped in **porous reservoir rocks** (like sandstone or limestone) situated beneath an **impermeable cap rock** (like shale or salt) that prevents the oil from escaping to the surface.

questions.question: What does a lens with a power of 1 dioptre indicate?

options.text: It has a focal length of 100 m.
It has a focal length of 1 metre.
It has a focal length of 1 cm.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has a focal length of 1 metre.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **power of a lens** is defined as the ability of a lens to converge or diverge light rays. Mathematically, it is the **reciprocal of its focal length**.
 
• The **SI unit** of power of a lens is the **dioptre**, which is denoted by the symbol **D**.
 
• The relationship between power (P) and focal length (f) is given by the formula **P = 1/f**, where the focal length must be measured in **metres**.
 
• By definition, **1 dioptre** is the power of a lens whose **focal length is 1 metre** (1 D = 1 m⁻¹). Hence, the statement in the question indicates a focal length of **1 metre**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 2.***
 
• The power of a lens is **positive** for a **converging (convex) lens** and **negative** for a **diverging (concave) lens**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Focal Length (f)**:
 
 
• It is the distance between the **optical centre** of the lens and the **principal focus**.
 
• If the focal length is given in **centimetres**, the power formula is modified to **P = 100/f (in cm)**. For example, a lens with a focal length of **25 cm** has a power of **+4 D**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention and Lens Types**:
 
 
• A **convex lens** has a real focus and thus a **positive focal length**, leading to a **positive power**.
 
• A **concave lens** has a virtual focus and a **negative focal length**, resulting in a **negative power**.
 
 
 
• **Power of a Combination of Lenses**:
 
 
• When two or more thin lenses are placed in contact, the total power (**P**) of the system is the **algebraic sum** of the individual powers: **P = P1 + P2 + P3 + ...**.
 
• This principle is used by **optometrists** to design corrective spectacles and by engineers in **telescopes** and **microscope** objectives.
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m)**:
 
 
• Unlike power, **magnification** is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (**m = h'/h**) or the ratio of image distance to object distance (**m = v/u**).
 
• It is a **unitless** quantity, whereas power has the unit of **m⁻¹** or **dioptre**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Corrective Lenses**: A person suffering from **Myopia** (nearsightedness) is prescribed a lens with **negative power** (concave), while someone with **Hypermetropia** (farsightedness) requires a lens with **positive power** (convex).
 
• **Optical Instruments**: The use of dioptre helps in the standardized manufacturing of **eye-glasses** and **contact lenses** globally. The **least distance of distinct vision** for a normal human eye is approximately **25 cm**.
 
• **Refractive Index**: The power of a lens also depends on the **refractive index** of the material it is made of and the **radii of curvature** of its surfaces, as described by the **Lens Maker's Formula**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a correct expression for electric power (P)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P = I × R²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric Power (P)** is defined as the rate at which **electrical energy** is consumed or dissipated in an electric circuit. It is the rate of doing work.
 
• The fundamental expression for **Electric Power** is the product of **Potential Difference (V)** and **Current (I)**, represented as **P = V × I**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance is given by **V = I × R**. By substituting **V** in the power formula (**P = VI**), we get **P = (I × R) × I**, which results in **P = I² × R**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Using **Ohm's Law** again, we can express current as **I = V / R**. By substituting **I** in the fundamental power formula (**P = VI**), we get **P = V × (V / R)**, which results in **P = V² / R**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The expression **P = I × R²** does not follow from any physical derivation of electrical laws and is dimensionally inconsistent with the units of power. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Therefore, **P = I × R²** is **NOT** a correct expression for electric power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit of Power**: The **SI unit** of electric power is the **Watt (W)**. It is named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt**. **1 Watt** is defined as the power consumed by a device when **1 Ampere** of current flows through it at a potential difference of **1 Volt**.
 
• **Ohm's Law**: Proposed by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the **voltage** across it, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant (**V = IR**).
 
• **Components of the Formula**:
 
 
• **V** stands for **Voltage** or **Potential Difference**, measured in **Volts (V)**.
 
• **I** stands for **Electric Current**, measured in **Amperes (A)**.
 
• **R** stands for **Resistance**, measured in **Ohms (Ω)**.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Unit of Energy**: While the **SI unit** of energy is the **Joule (J)**, the commercial unit is the **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**. **1 kWh** is the energy consumed by an appliance of **1000 Watts** in **one hour**. Numerically, **1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Joule's Law of Heating**: This law states that the heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the **square of the current**, the **resistance**, and the **time** for which the current flows (**H = I²Rt**). This is directly related to the power formula **P = I²R**.
 
• **Power in Series vs. Parallel**:
 
 
• In a **series circuit**, the **current (I)** remains constant. Thus, **P = I²R** is more convenient for calculations, showing power is directly proportional to **resistance**.
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the **voltage (V)** remains constant. Thus, **P = V² / R** is more convenient, showing power is inversely proportional to **resistance**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications**: These formulas are used to determine the **power rating** of household appliances like bulbs, heaters, and irons. For example, a bulb rated **100W, 220V** uses these relations to define its operational **resistance**.
</ul

questions.question: The work done by friction on a moving object is usually ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **work done** by a force on an object is defined as the product of the **component of the force** in the direction of the displacement and the **magnitude of the displacement**.
 
• Mathematically, work is expressed as **W = F × d × cosθ**, where **F** is the force magnitude, **d** is the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the **force vector** and the **displacement vector**.
 
• **Friction** is a force that **resists** the relative motion of solid surfaces, fluid layers, and material elements sliding against each other.
 
• When an object moves on a surface, **kinetic friction** acts in a direction **opposite** to the direction of the object's **displacement**.
 
• Because the force of friction and the displacement are in opposite directions, the **angle θ is 180 degrees**.
 
• Since the **cosine of 180 degrees is -1**, the resulting value of work is **negative**. ***Hence, the correct answer is negative.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Work:**
 
 
• **Positive Work**: Occurs when the force and displacement are in the **same direction** (angle between **0 and 90 degrees**). For example, work done by a person **pulling a cart**.
 
• **Negative Work**: Occurs when the force and displacement are in **opposite directions** (angle between **90 and 180 degrees**). Friction is the most common example.
 
• **Zero Work**: Occurs when the force is **perpendicular** to the displacement (angle is **90 degrees**) or if the **displacement is zero**. For instance, the **centripetal force** acting on a satellite does **zero work** because it is perpendicular to the motion.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Friction:**
 
 
• Friction is a **non-conservative force**, meaning the work done against it depends on the **path taken** rather than just the initial and final positions.
 
• The **coefficient of friction** (represented by the Greek letter **μ**) is a **dimensionless scalar value** that describes the ratio of the force of friction between two bodies and the **normal force** pressing them together.
 
• In almost all practical mechanical systems, friction converts **kinetic energy** into **thermal energy (heat)**, leading to energy dissipation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• While work done by friction is **usually negative**, it can be **positive** in certain frames of reference or specific scenarios. For example, if a **block A** is placed on top of **block B** and block B is accelerated, the friction exerted by B on A causes A to move. In this case, friction does **positive work** on block A because the force and displacement are in the **same direction**.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 Newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• The **Work-Energy Theorem** states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. Since friction usually does negative work, it typically **decreases** the kinetic energy of a moving object, causing it to **slow down**.

questions.question: Which of the following crosses will produce all heterozygous offspring in the F1 generation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TT × tt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A cross between **TT** (homozygous dominant) and **tt** (homozygous recessive) results in all offspring having the genotype **Tt**. This means **100%** of the **F1 generation** will be **heterozygous**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• In the cross **tt × tt**, both parents are **homozygous recessive**. They can only pass the **t** allele to their offspring, resulting in **100%** **homozygous recessive** (**tt**) individuals. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• In the cross **TT × TT**, both parents are **homozygous dominant**. They can only pass the **T** allele to their offspring, resulting in **100%** **homozygous dominant** (**TT**) individuals. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• In the cross **Tt × Tt**, both parents are **heterozygous**. According to **Mendelian genetics**, this cross produces a **genotypic ratio** of **1:2:1** (**25% TT**, **50% Tt**, and **25% tt**). Since only **50%** are heterozygous, they are not "all" heterozygous. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• This principle was first established by **Gregor Mendel** in his **1865** experiments with **pea plants** (**Pisum sativum**), forming the basis of the **Law of Segregation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heterozygous:** This refers to an individual having two different **alleles** for a particular gene, such as **Tt**. In such cases, the **dominant allele** (**T**) typically masks the expression of the **recessive allele** (**t**).
 
• **Homozygous:** This term describes an organism that has two identical **alleles** for a trait, which can be either **homozygous dominant** (**TT**) or **homozygous recessive** (**tt**).
 
• **Genotype and Phenotype:** The **genotype** is the actual genetic makeup (e.g., **Tt**), while the **phenotype** is the observable physical characteristic (e.g., **Tall** height). In an **F1 generation** of **Tt**, the phenotype is usually **100%** dominant.
 
• **Punnett Square:** This is a graphical representation used to calculate the probability of an offspring having a particular genotype. It was devised by **Reginald Punnett** in **1905**.
 
• **Monohybrid Cross:** This is a genetic cross between two individuals involving **one pair** of contrasting characters. The cross of **TT × tt** is a classic example of a monohybrid cross looking at plant height.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Dominance:** **Gregor Mendel** observed that in the **F1 generation**, only one of the parental traits (the **dominant** one) appears. For the cross **TT × tt**, although the offspring are **heterozygous**, they all appear **Tall**.

questions.question: Why do we see the flash of lightning before we hear the sound of thunder?

options.text: Light and sound travel at the same speed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sound travels slower than light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental reason we see lightning before hearing thunder is the vast difference in the **speed** at which light and sound travel through the **atmosphere**.
 
• **Light** travels at an incredible speed of approximately **300,000,000 meters per second** (or **3 x 10⁸ m/s**) in a vacuum and slightly slower in air. This speed is so high that for terrestrial distances, light appears to travel **instantaneously**.
 
• **Sound**, on the other hand, travels much slower, at about **343 meters per second** in dry air at a temperature of **20 degrees Celsius** (**68 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• When a lightning strike occurs, both the **optical flash** and the **acoustic shockwave** (thunder) are created at the exact same moment. However, because light is nearly **874,000 times faster** than sound, the visual information reaches the observer almost immediately, while the sound waves take several seconds to cover the same distance. ***Hence, the correct answer is Sound travels slower than light.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Light:**
 
 
• Light is an **electromagnetic wave** that does not require a **medium** to propagate. It can travel through the **vacuum** of outer space.
 
• In the context of a storm, the **photons** emitted by the electrical discharge of lightning move through the air with minimal resistance to their speed.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Sound:**
 
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave** (specifically a **longitudinal wave**) that requires a **medium** like air, water, or solids to travel.
 
• The speed of sound is highly dependent on the **density** and **temperature** of the medium. For instance, sound travels **faster in water** and even faster in **solids** like steel compared to its speed in air.
 
 
 
• **Distance Estimation:**
 
 
• Observers can estimate the distance of a storm using the **"flash-to-bang"** method. Since sound travels about **1 kilometer** every **3 seconds** (or 1 mile every 5 seconds), counting the delay between the flash and the thunder allows one to calculate how far away the lightning struck.
 
• If the delay is **9 seconds**, the lightning strike is approximately **3 kilometers** away.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Effect:** The speed of sound increases as the **temperature** of the air increases. At **0 degrees Celsius**, the speed of sound is about **331 m/s**, whereas at **30 degrees Celsius**, it increases to approximately **349 m/s**.
 
• **Sonic Boom:** When an object, such as a supersonic jet, travels faster than the **speed of sound** (Mach 1), it creates a **shockwave** similar to thunder, known as a **sonic boom**.
 
• **Lightning Composition:** A lightning bolt can heat the surrounding air to **30,000 Kelvin** (five times hotter than the surface of the sun). This sudden **thermal expansion** of air is what generates the sound wave we call **thunder**.
 
• **Refraction:** Sometimes, lightning can be seen but thunder is not heard; this is often called **"heat lightning."** This occurs because the sound waves are **refracted** (bent) upward by different temperature layers in the atmosphere before they can reach the observer's ears.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to separate particles from a suspension?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Filtration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Filtration** is a physical method used to separate **insoluble solid particles** from a liquid or gas by passing the mixture through a porous medium, such as **filter paper** or a **membrane**. Since the particles in a **suspension** are large enough to be trapped, this method is highly effective. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• A **suspension** is a **heterogeneous mixture** containing solid particles large enough for sedimentation. These particles are usually larger than **1000 nanometers** and are visible to the naked eye.
 
• In the filtration process, the clear liquid that passes through the filter is known as the **filtrate**, while the solid particles that remain on the filter medium are referred to as the **residue**.
 
• **Crystallization** is a technique used to separate a **pure solid** from a solution in the form of its **crystals**. It is commonly used for purification rather than simple mechanical separation of a suspension. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Distillation** is used to separate components of a mixture containing **miscible liquids** that boil without decomposition and have a significant difference in their **boiling points** (usually more than **25 K**). ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation** is a process used to separate a **non-volatile solute** (like salt) from a **volatile solvent** (like water) by heating the mixture until the liquid turns into **vapor**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Mixtures:**
 
 
• **Solution:** A **homogeneous mixture** of two or more substances where the particle size is less than **1 nm**. They do not scatter light and cannot be separated by filtration.
 
• **Colloid:** A mixture where the particle size (between **1 nm and 1000 nm**) is intermediate between a solution and a suspension. While they appear homogeneous, they are **heterogeneous** and exhibit the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• **Suspension:** A **heterogeneous mixture** where particles eventually **settle down** due to gravity if left undisturbed, making the mixture **unstable**.
 
 
 
• **Other Separation Techniques:**
 
 
• **Centrifugation:** Used when the solid particles are too small to be caught by a filter. The mixture is spun rapidly, forcing denser particles to the bottom. Examples include separating **cream from milk** or **diagnostic blood tests**.
 
• **Chromatography:** A technique used to separate solutes that dissolve in the **same solvent**, often used to separate **pigments from natural colors** or **drugs from blood**.
 
• **Sublimation:** Used to separate mixtures containing a **sublimable volatile component** (like **Ammonium chloride** or **Camphor**) from a non-sublimable impurity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Tyndall Effect** is the scattering of a beam of light by medium particles. It is clearly visible in **suspensions** and **colloids** but not in **true solutions**.
 
• The effectiveness of **Filtration** depends on the **pore size** of the filter medium and the **particle size** of the suspended matter.
 
• Unlike **Chemical separation**, methods like **Filtration**, **Evaporation**, and **Distillation** are **Physical separation** methods because they do not alter the chemical identity of the substances involved.
 
• Common examples of **Suspensions** include **Chalk powder in water**, **Muddy water**, and **Flour in water**.
</ul

questions.question: When an object is placed in a fluid, it feels an upward force called buoyancy. On which factor does the magnitude of this buoyant force depend?

options.text: The weight of the object only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The density of the fluid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **buoyant force**, also known as **upthrust**, is the upward force exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of a partially or fully immersed object.
 
• According to **Archimedes' Principle**, the magnitude of the **buoyant force** is exactly equal to the **weight of the fluid displaced** by the object.
 
• The formula for buoyant force is **Fb = ρ × V × g**, where **ρ (rho)** represents the **density of the fluid**, **V** represents the **volume of the displaced fluid**, and **g** represents the **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²**).
 
• The **density of the fluid** is a critical factor; for a fixed volume, a denser fluid (like **saltwater** compared to **freshwater**) will exert a greater upward force. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The **weight of the object** does not determine the magnitude of the buoyant force, though it determines whether the object will **sink or float** when compared to the buoyant force. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **color of the object** is a physical appearance property and has no physical interaction with fluid mechanics or pressure differentials. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **shape of the object** does not affect the buoyant force directly; only the **total volume** of the displaced fluid matters. Two objects of different shapes but the same volume will experience the same buoyant force if fully submerged. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' Principle:** Discovered in the **3rd Century BC** by the Greek mathematician **Archimedes of Syracuse**, this principle is the fundamental law of buoyancy used in **ship design** and **submarines**.
 
• **Sinking and Floating:** An object **sinks** if its **density** is greater than the density of the fluid. It **floats** if its density is less than the fluid's density. If the densities are equal, it exhibits **neutral buoyancy**.
 
• **Fluid Pressure:** Buoyancy arises because **fluid pressure** increases with **depth**. The pressure on the bottom of an submerged object is higher than the pressure on the top, resulting in a net upward force.
 
• **Real-world Example:** In the **Dead Sea**, the extremely high **salt concentration** increases the **density of the water** to about **1240 kg/m³**. This high density creates a massive **buoyant force**, allowing humans to float effortlessly on the surface.
 
• **Applications:** This concept is used in **Hydrometers** (to measure fluid density), **Lactometers** (to check the purity of milk), and the operation of **Hot Air Balloons** (where hot air is less dense than the surrounding cool air).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Apparent Weight:** When an object is immersed in a fluid, it appears to lose weight. The **apparent weight** is calculated as **Actual Weight - Buoyant Force**.
 
• **Volume Displacement:** For a fully submerged object, the **volume of displaced fluid** is equal to the **total volume** of the object. For a floating object, it is equal to the volume of the **submerged portion** only.
 
• **Relative Density:** Also known as **Specific Gravity**, it is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of a reference substance (usually **water** at **4 degrees Celsius**, which is **1000 kg/m³**).
 
• **Center of Buoyancy:** This is the **centroid** of the displaced volume of fluid. For a floating body to be stable, the relative positions of the **Center of Gravity** and the **Center of Buoyancy** are crucial.

8f:T2

questions.question: A food chain starts from grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk. How much concentration of non-biodegradable pesticides is expected in hawk?

options.text: The lowest amount of pesticide residue
Equal concentration of pesticide as in the frog

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The highest concentration of pesticides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biological Magnification**, also known as **Biomagnification**, is the process where the concentration of **non-biodegradable** toxic substances increases at each successive **trophic level** of a food chain.
 
• In the provided food chain: **Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk**, the **Hawk** occupies the **fifth trophic level** as the top predator.
 
• Since **pesticides** are often **non-biodegradable**, they are not broken down by the metabolic processes of organisms nor are they excreted easily. Instead, they accumulate in the fatty tissues of the organisms.
 
• As a predator eats multiple prey items from the level below it, it ingests all the accumulated toxins from those individuals. Consequently, the organism at the **highest trophic level** always ends up with the **maximum concentration** of these chemicals.
 
• Therefore, in this specific chain, the **Hawk** will exhibit the **highest concentration of pesticides** compared to the grass, grasshopper, frog, or snake. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Trophic Levels**:
 
 
• **First Trophic Level**: Consists of **Producers** like **Grass**, which have the **lowest concentration** of toxins as they are the entry point into the food web.
 
• **Intermediate Levels**: Includes **Primary Consumers** (Grasshopper), **Secondary Consumers** (Frog), and **Tertiary Consumers** (Snake). The concentration increases step-by-step through these levels.
 
• **Quaternary Consumers**: Represented here by the **Hawk**, which acts as the apex predator in this sequence.
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow vs. Biomagnification**:
 
 
• According to the **10% Law** proposed by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**, only **10%** of the **energy** is transferred to the next trophic level, while **90%** is lost as heat.
 
• Contrarily, **non-biodegradable chemicals** do not follow this reduction; their total mass remains largely the same while the biomass of the higher level is smaller, leading to a much higher **concentration**.
 
 
 
• **Common Pollutants**:
 
 
• **DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane)**: One of the most famous examples of a pesticide that causes **Biomagnification**. It was widely used in the **20th century** before being banned in many countries.
 
• **Heavy Metals**: Elements like **Mercury**, **Lead**, and **Cadmium** also undergo this process, often leading to conditions like **Minamata disease** in humans who consume high-level predatory fish.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Impact**:
 
 
• High concentrations of pesticides in birds of prey (like **Hawks** and **Eagles**) interfere with **calcium metabolism**, causing the **thinning of eggshells**. This leads to premature breaking of eggs and a significant decline in bird populations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biodegradable vs. Non-biodegradable**: Only **non-biodegradable** substances (those that cannot be decomposed by biological processes) undergo **Biomagnification**. **Biodegradable** substances are broken down and do not accumulate.
 
• **Bioaccumulation**: This refers to the build-up of a substance in a **single organism's** body over time, whereas **Biomagnification** refers to the increase in concentration across **multiple levels** of the food chain.
 
• **Human Impact**: Humans, being **omnivores** and often occupying the **top of the food chain**, are highly susceptible to the effects of **biological magnification** through the consumption of meat, fish, and dairy.
</ul

questions.question: A current I ampere flows through a metallic wire of resistance X Omega when a potential difference V volt is applied across its ends. Which of the following is the correct relation between X, I and V ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**X = V/I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law**, discovered by the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, provides the fundamental relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.
 
• According to this law, the **potential difference (V)** across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the **current (I)** flowing through it, provided its **temperature** remains constant.
 
• Mathematically, this relationship is expressed as **V = I × R**, where **R** is a constant for the given metallic wire at a given temperature and is called its **resistance**.
 
• In the given question, the resistance is denoted by **X**. Therefore, the equation becomes **V = I × X**.
 
• To find the relation for **X**, we rearrange the formula as **X = V / I**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The relationship is linear, meaning if the **potential difference** is doubled, the **current** also doubles, keeping the ratio **V/I** (the resistance) constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Resistance (X)**:
 
 
• It is the property of a conductor to **oppose the flow of electric current**.
 
• The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, denoted by the Greek symbol **Ω**.
 
• **1 Ohm** is defined as the resistance of a conductor when a potential difference of **1 Volt** applied across its ends results in a current of **1 Ampere** flowing through it.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance**:
 
 
• The resistance of a uniform metallic conductor is **directly proportional** to its **length (L)**.
 
• It is **inversely proportional** to the **area of cross-section (A)**.
 
• It depends on the **nature of the material** (resistivity) and the **temperature** of the conductor. For most metals, resistance **increases** with an increase in temperature.
 
 
 
• **Potential Difference (V)**:
 
 
• It is the work done to move a **unit charge** from one point to another in an electric field. The **SI unit** is the **Volt**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Current (I)**:
 
 
• It is the **rate of flow of electric charges** through a cross-section of a conductor. The **SI unit** is the **Ampere**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **V-I Graph**: For a conductor that obeys **Ohm's Law** (an **Ohmic conductor**), the graph of potential difference (V) versus current (I) is a **straight line passing through the origin**. The **slope** of this line represents the **resistance** of the conductor.
 
• **Ohmic vs. Non-Ohmic**: Materials like metals are generally **Ohmic** at stable temperatures. However, components like **diodes**, **transistors**, and **vacuum tubes** do not follow a linear relationship and are called **Non-Ohmic** conductors.
 
• **Application of the Formula**: The formula **V = IX** is crucial for calculating the necessary **voltage** or **current** in electrical circuits, designing household wiring, and determining the power consumption of appliances.
 
• **Formula Variations**:
 
 
• To find Current: **I = V / X**
 
• To find Voltage: **V = I × X**
 
• To find Resistance: **X = V / I**
 
 
</ul

questions.question: A rainbow is formed in the sky after rain, which is due to _______________.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**refraction and dispersion of light by raindrops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A rainbow is a **meteorological phenomenon** that is caused by **reflection**, **refraction**, and **dispersion** of light in water droplets resulting in a spectrum of light appearing in the sky.
 
• When sunlight strikes a **raindrop**, it is first **refracted** as it enters the surface of the droplet. This causes the white light to slow down and bend.
 
• During this process, **dispersion** occurs, where the white sunlight is split into its component colors (**VIBGYOR**) because different wavelengths of light travel at different speeds within the water.
 
• The light then hits the back of the raindrop and undergoes **internal reflection**. After reflecting, the light is **refracted** once more as it exits the droplet, further spreading the colors.
 
• The combined effect of these optical processes—**refraction**, **dispersion**, and **reflection**—directs the light toward the observer's eye at specific angles (approximately **40 to 42 degrees**), forming a circular arc of colors. ***Hence, the correct answer is refraction and dispersion of light by raindrops.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Visible Spectrum (VIBGYOR):** The colors in a rainbow always appear in a specific order: **Violet**, **Indigo**, **Blue**, **Green**, **Yellow**, **Orange**, and **Red**. **Red light** has the **longest wavelength** and is refracted the least, appearing on the **outer arc**. **Violet light** has the **shortest wavelength** and is refracted the most, appearing on the **inner arc**.
 
• **Conditions for Formation:** For a rainbow to be visible, two conditions must be met simultaneously: the **Sun** must be shining in one part of the sky, and it must be **raining** (or water droplets must be present) in the opposite part of the sky. The observer must stand with their **back to the Sun**.
 
• **Primary vs. Secondary Rainbows:** A **Primary Rainbow** is formed by **one internal reflection** inside the raindrop. A **Secondary Rainbow** is formed when light undergoes **two internal reflections**. The secondary rainbow is fainter, appears outside the primary arc, and its color sequence is **reversed** (Red on the inside, Violet on the outside).
 
• **Shape of a Rainbow:** While we usually see a rainbow as an arc from the ground, it is actually a **full circle**. The ground usually obstructs the bottom half of the circle. However, observers in **airplanes** or at high altitudes can sometimes see a **complete circular rainbow**.
 
• **Historical Context:** **Sir Isaac Newton** was the first to demonstrate in the **17th century** (specifically around **1666**) that white light is composed of a **spectrum of colors** by using a **glass prism**, which mimics the dispersive behavior of raindrops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Refraction:** This is the **bending of light** when it passes from one medium (like air) to another medium of different density (like water). The **refractive index** of water is approximately **1.33**.
 
• **Dispersion:** This is the **separation of white light** into colors of different **frequencies** and **wavelengths**. This happens because the **velocity** of light in a medium depends on its wavelength.
 
• **Total Internal Reflection:** While a portion of light undergoes **internal reflection** at the back of the raindrop to form a rainbow, it is important to note that it is often technically partial reflection, though it is the primary reason the light returns toward the observer.

Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

**Assertion (A): **Sexual reproduction is essential in plants for maintaining the continuity of the species for many generations.
**Reason (R): **Sexual reproduction leads to genetic variation that enhances adaptability and evolutionary fitness.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that **sexual reproduction** is essential in plants for maintaining the **continuity of the species** for many generations. Reproduction is a fundamental biological process that ensures **life** continues beyond the lifespan of an individual organism. *Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.*

• The **genetic diversity** created through sexual reproduction is the primary mechanism that allows a **plant population** to survive environmental changes, such as **climate shifts**, **new pathogens**, or **predators**.
 
• Because these variations allow the **species** to adapt and evolve over **geological time**, it directly enables the long-term **continuity** mentioned in the assertion. Without such variation, a species would be highly vulnerable to **extinction**. *Therefore, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Variation:** During **sexual reproduction**, variation arises primarily during **meiosis** through processes like **crossing over** (in **Prophase I**) and **independent assortment** of chromosomes. This reshuffles the **genetic material**, ensuring no two offspring (except identical twins) are exactly alike.
 
• **Evolutionary Fitness:** This term refers to an organism's ability to **survive** and **reproduce** in a specific environment. **Natural selection** acts on the **genetic variation** produced by sexual reproduction, preserving traits that improve a plant's chances of passing its **genes** to the next generation.
 
• **Comparison with Asexual Reproduction:** In **asexual reproduction** (such as **vegetative propagation**), offspring are **genetically identical** clones of the parent. While this is efficient for rapid **colonization**, the lack of **diversity** means the entire population could be wiped out by a single environmental stressor.
 
• **Significance in Plants:** For **Angiosperms** (flowering plants) and **Gymnosperms**, sexual reproduction results in the formation of **seeds**. Seeds often contain **dormant embryos** and protective coats, allowing the **species** to survive unfavorable seasons and disperse to new **geographical locations**.
 
• **Pollination and Fertilization:** These are the two critical steps in plant sexual reproduction. **Pollination** involves the transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** to the **stigma**, while **fertilization** is the fusion of male and female **gametes** to form a **zygote**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DNA Recombination:** This is the production of **offspring** with combinations of traits that differ from those found in either parent, serving as the raw material for **evolution**.
 
• **Species Continuity:** This refers to the uninterrupted **lineage** of a group of organisms. **Sexual reproduction** provides the **flexibility** required for a lineage to persist across **millions of years** despite the Earth's changing **ecology**.
 
• **Biological Stability:** While individual plants die, the process of **meiosis** and **syngamy** (fertilization) ensures that the **gene pool** remains dynamic and resilient.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about average speed is INCORRECT?

options.text: It is total distance divided by total time.
It does not depend on the direction of motion.
It is change in distance divided by change in velocity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is change in distance divided by change in velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average speed** is defined as the **total distance** traveled by an object divided by the **total time** interval taken to cover that distance. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The standard unit of measurement for speed in the **International System of Units (SI)** is **meters per second (m/s)**, although it can also be expressed in **km/h** or **miles per hour** depending on the context. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Speed is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it possesses only **magnitude** and no **directional component**. Therefore, the average speed of an object does not change based on the direction in which the object is moving. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The mathematical expression for average speed is **Total Distance / Total Time**. Defining it as the change in distance divided by the **change in velocity** is scientifically incorrect and has no physical basis in kinematics. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the incorrect statement (and thus the correct answer) is It is change in distance divided by change in velocity.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scalar vs Vector Quantities:**
 
 
• A **scalar quantity** like **speed** or **distance** is described solely by its numerical value.
 
• A **vector quantity** like **velocity** or **displacement** requires both **magnitude** and **direction** for a complete description.
 
• If a car travels in a **circular path** and returns to its starting point, its **average velocity** is **0** because the **net displacement** is **0**, but its **average speed** will be a positive **numerical value**.
 
 
 
• **Instantaneous Speed:**
 
 
• This refers to the speed of an object at a **specific point in time** or at a particular **instant**.
 
• The **speedometer** in vehicles is the primary tool used to measure **instantaneous speed**.
 
 
 
• **Unit Conversions:**
 
 
• To convert speed from **kilometers per hour (km/h)** to **meters per second (m/s)**, we multiply the value by **5/18**.
 
• To convert **m/s** back to **km/h**, the value is multiplied by **18/5**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for speed is represented as **[M0 L1 T-1]**, where **M** is mass, **L** is length, and **T** is time.
 
• **Odometer:** While the **speedometer** measures speed, the **odometer** is the device used to measure the total **distance** traveled by a vehicle.
 
• **Uniform Motion:** In **uniform motion**, an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, meaning its **speed** remains **constant** throughout the journey.
 
• **Average Velocity Formula:** Unlike average speed, **average velocity** is calculated as **Total Displacement / Total Time**. Because **displacement** is the shortest path between two points, the **magnitude** of average velocity is always **less than or equal to** average speed.
</ul

questions.question: Which alcohol is commonly used as fuel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethanol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol**, also known as **ethyl alcohol** (chemical formula **C2H5OH**), is the most common alcohol used as a **biofuel** worldwide.
 
• It is a **renewable** energy source because it is primarily produced through the **fermentation** of sugars and starches found in plant materials such as **sugarcane**, **corn**, **maize**, and **wheat**.
 
• In many countries, including **India**, **Brazil**, and the **USA**, ethanol is blended with **gasoline** (petrol) to reduce the consumption of fossil fuels and lower **carbon emissions**.
 
• The **Government of India** has launched the **Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme**, which initially targeted **5%** blending but has been scaled up significantly over the years.
 
• As a fuel, ethanol has a higher **octane rating** than pure gasoline, which helps improve engine performance and prevents **engine knocking**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Methanol (CH3OH)**:
 
 
• Also known as **wood alcohol**, it can be used as a fuel, particularly in **racing cars** and high-performance engines.
 
• While it is cheaper to produce from **coal** or **natural gas**, it is highly **toxic** and more **corrosive** to engine components than ethanol.
 
 
 
• **Butanol (C4H9OH)**:
 
 
• It is considered an advanced **biofuel** with an energy density very close to that of **gasoline**.
 
• Unlike ethanol, butanol is less **hydroscopic** (absorbs less water) and can be transported through existing **oil pipelines**, though its production cost remains high.
 
 
 
• **Propanol (C3H7OH)**:
 
 
• Commonly used as a **solvent** and in **antiseptics** (rubbing alcohol), but it is not typically used as a bulk commercial fuel due to production costs and chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **Flex-Fuel Vehicles (FFVs)**:
 
 
• These are specialized vehicles equipped with internal combustion engines designed to run on more than one fuel, usually gasoline blended with ethanol (up to **85%** or **E85**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's E20 Target**: The **Government of India** has advanced the target of achieving **20% ethanol blending** in petrol from **2030** to **2025-26** to reduce **import dependency** on crude oil.
 
• **National Policy on Biofuels (2018)**: This policy categorizes biofuels into **First Generation (1G)** bio-ethanol (from molasses, sugar beet, etc.) and **Second Generation (2G)** ethanol (from non-food crops and agricultural residues).
 
• **Global Biofuels Alliance (GBA)**: Launched during the **G20 Summit** in **2023** under India’s presidency, this alliance aims to accelerate the global uptake of **biofuels** like ethanol to support the **energy transition**.
 
• **Environmental Impact**: Using ethanol-blended fuels significantly reduces the emission of **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Hydrocarbons (HC)**, and **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)**, contributing to cleaner air in urban areas.

questions.question: Plastids are absent in which of the following cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscle cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plastids** are double-membrane-bound organelles found primarily in the cells of **plants** and **algae**. They are responsible for manufacturing and storing important chemical compounds used by the cell.
 
• **Muscle cells** are **animal cells**, and one of the fundamental differences between plant and animal cells is the presence of plastids. Animal cells, including human muscle cells, **lack plastids** entirely because they do not perform photosynthesis or require specialized plant storage structures like leucoplasts. ***Hence, the correct answer is Muscle cells.***
 
• **Leaf cells** (specifically the mesophyll cells) contain a high density of a specific type of plastid known as **chloroplasts**. These contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which captures light energy for **photosynthesis**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect as plastids are present.***
 
• **Stem cells** in plants, particularly in herbaceous or young stems, contain plastids such as **chloroplasts** or **proplastids** (precursors to other plastids). These allow the stem to contribute to the plant's energy production. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect as plastids are present.***
 
• **Root cells** also contain plastids, typically in the form of **leucoplasts**. Since roots are generally underground and not exposed to light, they do not require chloroplasts but use **amyloplasts** (a type of leucoplast) to store **starch**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect as plastids are present.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Plastids:**
 
 
• **Chloroplasts:** These are the most well-known plastids, containing **chlorophyll** and **carotenoid** pigments. They are the site of **photosynthesis**, converting light energy into chemical energy in the form of **glucose**.
 
• **Chromoplasts:** These contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like **carotene** and **xanthophylls**. They provide the distinct **yellow, orange, or red colors** to flowers and ripening fruits, aiding in pollination and seed dispersal.
 
• **Leucoplasts:** These are colorless plastids of varied shapes and sizes that store nutrients. They are further divided into:
 
 
• **Amyloplasts:** Specialized for storing **carbohydrates (starch)**, commonly found in **potato tubers** and **grains**.
 
• **Elaioplasts:** Responsible for storing **oils and fats**.
 
• **Aleuroplasts (Proteinoplasts):** Responsible for storing **proteins**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Semi-autonomous Nature:**
 
 
• Like mitochondria, plastids are **semi-autonomous organelles**. They possess their own **circular DNA** and **70S ribosomes**, allowing them to synthesize some of their own proteins and replicate independently within the cell.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• Scientific evidence suggests that plastids originated from **cyanobacteria** that entered into a symbiotic relationship with early eukaryotic cells roughly **1.5 billion years ago**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Internal Structure:** The inside of a chloroplast is organized into a matrix called the **stroma**, which contains membrane-bound sacs called **thylakoids**. These thylakoids are stacked like coins to form **grana** (singular: granum).
 
• **Pigment Distribution:** While all plastids derive from **proplastids**, their final form depends on the tissue **location** and exposure to **environmental factors** like light. For instance, if a root (containing leucoplasts) is exposed to light, it may turn green as the plastids develop into chloroplasts.
 
• **Functions:** Beyond energy production and storage, plastids play vital roles in the synthesis of **fatty acids**, **amino acids**, and **terpenes**, which are essential for the plant's survival and defense mechanisms.
</ul
